nodes.boundary: The cited method uses approximations and soft state constraints; globally optimal safe exploration is not established. [Scope reference](https://ei.is.mpg.de/uploads_file/attachment/attachment/341/dual_control_final.pdf)
nodes.test: Compare with random excitation and certainty-equivalent control at matched data, action cost, and enforced constraints.

nodes.name: Training dynamics as a control problem
nodes.authors: Hennick · De Baerdemacker; Hoogland et al.
nodes.text: Optimizer dynamics admit local response measurements and training interventions. Patterning and data/reward shaping demonstrate bounded changes, not general capability controllability.
nodes.handle: Recent SLT work studies SGD under specific local diffusion assumptions; stagewise studies motivate prospective intervention experiments. [Research reference](https://proceedings.iclr.cc/paper_files/paper/2026/file/a7b562dac391e9c7af691e8ef886ad10-Paper-Conference.pdf) Patterning supplies empirical data-reweighting interventions beyond passive diagnostics. [Wang and Murfet](https://arxiv.org/html/2601.13548v1)
nodes.boundary: The cited results do not establish general controllability of Adam, a trained model's capabilities, or semantic alignment. [Scope reference](https://proceedings.iclr.cc/paper_files/paper/2026/file/a7b562dac391e9c7af691e8ef886ad10-Paper-Conference.pdf)
nodes.test: Pre-register data/curriculum interventions and compare response prediction against validation-loss, gradient and random-schedule baselines.

nodes.name: HiPPO: designed memory dynamics
nodes.authors: Albert Gu · Tri Dao · Stefano Ermon · Atri Rudra · Christopher Ré
nodes.text: Online polynomial projections of signal history yield structured recurrent memory updates. A constructive bridge from approximation theory to long-memory learning.
nodes.handle: Design memory through a specified history measure and projection dynamics, rather than rely only on unconstrained recurrent optimization. [Evidence](https://hazyresearch.stanford.edu/blog/2020-12-05-hippo)
nodes.boundary: Benchmark gains are not evidence of general LLM training efficiency. Memory representation and desired semantics are separate targets. [Scope](https://hazyresearch.stanford.edu/blog/2020-12-05-hippo)
nodes.test: Compare learned long-range tasks with matched parameters, total tuning/training cost, memory length, and held-out sequence lengths.

nodes.name: LRU: stable linear recurrent units
nodes.authors: Antonio Orvieto · Samuel L. Smith · Albert Gu · Anushan Fernando · Caglar Gulcehre · Razvan Pascanu · Soham De
nodes.text: Complex diagonal linear recurrence, stable initialization, normalization and parallel scans support long-sequence learning. The complete network still contains nonlinear components.
nodes.handle: The tested tanh-RNN comparison reports 1.9–29× training-step throughput across tasks, with 94.2% PathX accuracy for LRU. [Evidence](https://proceedings.mlr.press/v202/orvieto23a/orvieto23a.pdf)
nodes.boundary: Faster steps do not imply the same speedup to a fixed capability. These are task- and hardware-specific comparisons, not dominance over every SSM or Transformer. [Scope](https://proceedings.mlr.press/v202/orvieto23a/orvieto23a.pdf)
nodes.test: Measure total cost to a fixed held-out capability, including tuning, and compare correction retention and rare-task learning.

nodes.name: Patterning: developmental training interventions
nodes.text: Estimate susceptibility of posterior observables to training-distribution changes, then reweight data to influence which solution is learned.
nodes.handle: The parentheses experiment changes solution selection: mean out-of-distribution accuracy .310 → .497 in the favorable condition. LLC is one target observable. [Evidence](https://arxiv.org/html/2601.13548v1)
nodes.boundary: This is bounded developmental intervention, not established net efficiency. Language-model susceptibility estimation costs about 500× model training by forward-pass accounting; uniform training has the lowest loss. [Scope](https://arxiv.org/html/2601.13548v1)
nodes.test: Compare against gradient alignment and simple curricula at equal total compute, including all susceptibility sampling.

nodes.name: Goodfire: predictive data & reward shaping
nodes.authors: Leon Bergen · Usha Bhalla · Sidharth Baskaran · Max Loeffler · Ekdeep Singh Lubana et al.
nodes.text: Anatomy of Post-Training predicts concept changes from preference examples and changes the learning signal to suppress or amplify selected behaviors.
nodes.handle: Targeted poetic reward shaping gains about 40 Elo on Creative Writing Bench v3. Feature-conditioned prediction has R²=.90; prompt-conditioned prediction has R²=.58. [Evidence](https://arxiv.org/html/2606.12360v1)
nodes.boundary: Concept changes are not arbitrary capability prediction. Full discovery, probe, and training cost is not established as a net efficiency win; correlated concepts limit independent shaping. [Scope](https://arxiv.org/html/2606.12360v1)
nodes.test: Prospectively predict held-out training changes, then compare targeted quality gains against simple data filtering at matched total cost.

nodes.name: Goodfire: features as RL rewards
nodes.authors: Aaditya Prasad · Connor Watts · Jack Merullo · Dhruvil Gala · Owen Lewis · Thomas McGrath · Ekdeep Singh Lubana
nodes.text: Learned feedback from probes on a frozen model supplies inexpensive rewards while a separate model is trained. The atlas covers supervision and behavioral results, not circuit reconstruction.
nodes.handle: Reported Gemma 3 12B training budget buys 360 optimizer steps versus 3–5 with the compared Gemini-plus-web feedback pipeline. [Evidence](https://www.goodfire.com/research/rlfr)
nodes.boundary: The headline 58% hallucination reduction includes intervention and best-of-32 selection. It is not a training-only gain, and full probe-construction cost must be counted. [Scope](https://www.goodfire.com/research/rlfr)
nodes.test: Separate trained-policy, monitor, selection, and combined performance; compare total supervision plus training and inference cost.

nodes.name: Goodfire: probe-based data attribution
nodes.text: Align preference-example representation differences with a behavior probe, rank data, then edit the dataset and retrain.
nodes.handle: Filtering the top 30,000 examples reduces the tested harmful-distractor compliance by 63%; ranking is reported at 12 H100-hours versus 128 for a gradient comparator, after probe training. [Evidence](https://www.goodfire.com/research/probe-based-data-attribution)
nodes.boundary: A targeted correction and ranking-cost reduction are not proof of more general capability or end-to-end compute efficiency. [Scope](https://www.goodfire.com/research/probe-based-data-attribution)
nodes.test: Compare probe ranking, gradient alignment, simple metadata rules, and random filtering on prospective response and held-out task utility.

nodes.name: Gradient interference & rare-task retention
nodes.authors: Jing Huang · Daniel Wurgaft · Rachit Bansal · Laura Ruis · Naomi Saphra · David Alvarez-Melis · Andrew Lampinen · Christopher Potts · Ekdeep Singh Lubana
nodes.text: Common-task updates can overwrite rare-task learning. Capacity, task frequency, and example spacing affect whether weak learning signals accumulate.
nodes.handle: Synthetic and language-model experiments vary size, frequency and spacing; fitting common tasks reduces interfering residual gradients in the proposed account. [Evidence](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2605.29548)
nodes.boundary: The work does not establish a universally efficient gradient-surgery optimizer. A capacity explanation is not yet a cost-matched replay-controller result. [Scope](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2605.29548)
nodes.test: At fixed examples and total compute, test interference-aware spacing and replay against uniform sampling and loss-based prioritization.

nodes.name: μP & μTransfer
nodes.authors: Greg Yang · Edward J. Hu and collaborators
nodes.text: Width-aware parameterization supports transfer of tuned hyperparameters from small models to larger models.
nodes.handle: A reported 40M-to-6.7B model transfer uses tuning compute equivalent to 7% of the large model's pretraining budget. [Evidence](https://www.microsoft.com/en-us/research/publication/tuning-large-neural-networks-via-zero-shot-hyperparameter-transfer/)
nodes.boundary: This is tuning efficiency, not a claim that the large model needs only 7% of its original training compute or that semantic behavior becomes controllable. [Scope](https://www.microsoft.com/en-us/research/publication/tuning-large-neural-networks-via-zero-shot-hyperparameter-transfer/)
nodes.test: Test hyperparameter transfer, failed-run cost, and final held-out quality under the actual architecture and scale changes.

nodes.name: Our work: typed-control response prediction
nodes.text: A Qwen3-1.7B LoRA experiment predicts observable changes from data reweighting. It is a forward-response benchmark, not demonstrated inverse capability control.
nodes.handle: Median linear datamodeling score across seven observables: gradient alignment .72; tested GGN −.14; empirical Fisher .05. [Evidence](https://github.com/apumutyala/chl-typed-control/issues/1#issuecomment-5925146688)
nodes.boundary: SGLD .03 is inconclusive with insufficient sampling/convergence evidence. This is not a general disproof of susceptibility methods or SLT. [Scope](https://github.com/apumutyala/chl-typed-control/issues/1#issuecomment-5925146688)
nodes.test: Select interventions from predicted responses and test held-out capability gain and retention at equal total cost.

nodes.name: Our work: state-space qualification
nodes.text: Executable L0–L4 gates prepare evaluation of qualified native RWKV7 parent models, including task capability, retention and intervention controls.
nodes.handle: The reviewed PR prepares capability and intervention evaluation with same-task comparators, sham, random, and output-only controls. [Evidence](https://github.com/apumutyala/State-Space-Decision-Model/pull/215)
nodes.boundary: PR 215 is readiness evidence, not a qualified learned-capability result. Its hidden-feature intervention does not establish recurrent-memory control. [Scope](https://github.com/apumutyala/State-Space-Decision-Model/pull/215)
nodes.test: Qualify a learned parent first, then evaluate actual memory-state interventions and persistent task correction.

nodes.name: Our work: structured model construction
nodes.text: The project brief distinguishes intentionally structured architecture and training from retrofitting controls onto a finished black-box model.
nodes.handle: Treat construction from initialization as the main track and keep retrofit experiments separate. [Evidence](https://github.com/apumutyala/chl-structured-models/issues/1)
nodes.boundary: A project objective is not a successful capability or alignment result; benchmark claims require their own experiment records. [Scope](https://github.com/apumutyala/chl-structured-models/issues/1)
nodes.test: Cross architectural structure with response-aware training and report capability, correction retention, and full compute cost.

nodes.name: Sampling, aliasing & anti-aliasing
nodes.text: Sampling can make distinct continuous signals indistinguishable. Band limits and anti-alias filters determine what a measurement stream can preserve.
nodes.handle: Choose acquisition rate, filtering and units before fitting the downstream model. [Reference](https://ocw.mit.edu/courses/2-161-signal-processing-continuous-and-discrete-fall-2008/80ec6fb9bd027f30adcdc16577e8ab16_samplingdft.pdf)
nodes.boundary: Nyquist reconstruction assumes an appropriate band-limited signal. Better inference cannot uniquely recover arbitrary information lost through aliasing. [Scope](https://ocw.mit.edu/courses/2-161-signal-processing-continuous-and-discrete-fall-2008/80ec6fb9bd027f30adcdc16577e8ab16_samplingdft.pdf)
nodes.test: Vary sample rate and sensor bandwidth; test whether action-relevant events remain distinguishable.

nodes.name: Spectral estimation & Welch averaging
nodes.text: Estimate signal power across frequency from finite records, trading spectral resolution against estimator variance through windowing and averaging.
nodes.handle: Use autocorrelation and spectral estimates to measure timescales, residual structure and oscillation. [Reference](https://ocw.mit.edu/courses/2-161-signal-processing-continuous-and-discrete-fall-2008/c7d1951d44fe78ea97d0e14ea5158aee_lecture_23.pdf)
nodes.boundary: Stationarity, finite-window bias and dependence between segments matter. A peak is not evidence of a causal mechanism or useful model state. [Scope](https://ocw.mit.edu/courses/2-161-signal-processing-continuous-and-discrete-fall-2008/c7d1951d44fe78ea97d0e14ea5158aee_lecture_23.pdf)
nodes.test: Compare estimated spectra and residual correlations against simulated ground truth and changes in operating regime.

nodes.name: Adaptive filtering: LMS & RLS
nodes.authors: Christian Feldbauer · Franz Pernkopf · Erhard Rank (tutorial)
nodes.text: Update linear filter coefficients online from a reference error; RLS uses recursively updated weighted least-squares information.
nodes.handle: LMS connects sample-gradient learning with adaptive FIR filters. RLS supplies a cheap online identification baseline. [Reference](https://www2.spsc.tugraz.at/www-archive/downloads/adaptivefilter.pdf)
nodes.boundary: The desired signal must be specified; learning-rate, excitation and tracking assumptions matter. Tracking a reference is not learning human intent. [Scope](https://www2.spsc.tugraz.at/www-archive/downloads/adaptivefilter.pdf)
nodes.test: Compare LMS, normalized LMS, RLS and a neural adapter on drifting systems at equal latency and labeled-data cost.

nodes.name: Wavelet scattering representations
nodes.text: Cascade wavelet convolutions, modulus and averaging to construct representations with specified invariance and deformation stability.
nodes.handle: Combine designed signal features with SVM or PCA classifiers; the paper reports both routes. [Reference](https://arxiv.org/abs/1203.1513)
nodes.boundary: The chosen invariance must preserve task distinctions. Representation stability does not imply semantic correctness or control stability. [Scope](https://arxiv.org/abs/1203.1513)
nodes.test: Compare scattering, learned CNN features and raw signals under physically relevant nuisance changes and task-changing perturbations.

nodes.name: Compressed sensing & sparse recovery
nodes.text: Recover sparse or compressible signals from underdetermined measurements under conditions on the sensing operator.
nodes.handle: Use sparsity and restricted-isometry/incoherence conditions to obtain specified recovery guarantees. [Reference](https://candes.su.domains/publications/downloads/CompressiveSampling.pdf)
nodes.boundary: A latent representation is not automatically sparse in the right basis; arbitrary measurement operators do not inherit recovery bounds. [Scope](https://candes.su.domains/publications/downloads/CompressiveSampling.pdf)
nodes.test: Check sensing assumptions, noise and sparsity mismatch before comparing learned reconstruction to sparse recovery.

nodes.name: Particle filtering
nodes.text: Approximate nonlinear filtering distributions with weighted samples rather than a single Gaussian approximation.
nodes.handle: Track multimodal beliefs when linear-Gaussian filtering is inadequate. [Reference](https://users.aalto.fi/~ssarkka/pub/bfs_book_2023_online.pdf)
nodes.boundary: Finite-particle degeneracy, model mismatch and high dimension can make uncertainty estimates misleading. [Scope](https://users.aalto.fi/~ssarkka/pub/bfs_book_2023_online.pdf)
nodes.test: Compare Kalman variants and particle filters with known hidden state, multimodal ambiguity and equal computational budgets.

nodes.name: Bayesian smoothing & retrospective state inference
nodes.text: Infer an earlier hidden state using observations that arrive later; filtering uses only observations available at the current time.
nodes.handle: Use forward-backward or state-space smoothing for offline learning and state reconstruction. [Reference](https://www.cs.ubc.ca/~murphyk/Thesis/thesis_double.pdf)
nodes.boundary: Using smoothed state as an online input leaks future information unless the deployment has the same delay. [Scope](https://www.cs.ubc.ca/~murphyk/Thesis/thesis_double.pdf)
nodes.test: Separate causal filtering from offline smoothing and audit timestamps in every forecast/control comparison.

nodes.name: Data assimilation & ensemble Kalman filters
nodes.text: Propagate an ensemble through a dynamical model, then assimilate observations using ensemble covariance estimates.
nodes.handle: Couple physics or learned forecasts with noisy measurements rather than running open-loop indefinitely. [Reference](https://www.ecmwf.int/sites/default/files/elibrary/2003/9321-ensemble-kalman-filter-theoretical-formulation-and-practical-implementation.pdf)
nodes.boundary: Finite ensembles and Gaussian-style updates are approximations for nonlinear systems; ensemble spread is not automatically calibrated coverage. [Scope](https://www.ecmwf.int/sites/default/files/elibrary/2003/9321-ensemble-kalman-filter-theoretical-formulation-and-practical-implementation.pdf)
nodes.test: Measure innovation consistency, forecast error, spread and closed-loop performance under sensor loss and model bias.

nodes.name: Logistic regression & generalized linear models
nodes.text: Use a link function to connect linear features with conditional probabilities, counts or other exponential-family responses.
nodes.handle: Build cheap, inspectable task and behavioral-surrogate baselines before adding nonlinear complexity. [Reference](https://scikit-learn.org/stable/modules/linear_model.html)
nodes.boundary: Coefficients depend on representation, regularization and data; a probability output is not automatically calibrated or causal. [Scope](https://scikit-learn.org/stable/modules/linear_model.html)
nodes.test: Compare accuracy, log score, calibration and correction response with neural predictors on identical features.

nodes.name: Lasso, elastic-net & sparse regularization
nodes.text: Penalize coefficient size with L1 or combined L1/L2 terms to encourage sparse or stabilized predictors.
nodes.handle: Connect sparse regression to compressed sensing and sparse dynamical-model identification. [Reference](https://scikit-learn.org/stable/modules/linear_model.html)
nodes.boundary: Sparsity is coordinate dependent; selected features need not be true causes or semantically sufficient. [Scope](https://scikit-learn.org/stable/modules/linear_model.html)
nodes.test: Compare sparse, ridge and unregularized models under correlated predictors and shifted interventions.

nodes.name: PCA & probabilistic factor analysis
nodes.text: Represent covariance through low-dimensional components; probabilistic factor analysis specifies latent Gaussian factors and observation noise.
nodes.handle: Use low-rank statistical baselines for compression and observation models. [Reference](https://scikit-learn.org/stable/modules/decomposition.html)
nodes.boundary: High variance is not the same as decision relevance, observability or controllability. Factor coordinates can remain ambiguous. [Scope](https://scikit-learn.org/stable/modules/decomposition.html)
nodes.test: Compare PCA against task-aware and balanced reduction on rare constraints and action-conditioned prediction.

nodes.name: ICA & blind source separation
nodes.text: Separate additive signal components using statistical independence assumptions rather than only uncorrelated directions.
nodes.handle: Model superimposed sensor sources and compare independent-component features with PCA features. [Reference](https://scikit-learn.org/stable/modules/decomposition.html)
nodes.boundary: Independence assumptions and remaining representation ambiguities do not identify arbitrary physical causes or semantic factors. [Scope](https://scikit-learn.org/stable/modules/decomposition.html)
nodes.test: Mix known sources, vary dependence and noise, and test whether recovered components support unseen interventions.

nodes.name: Gaussian mixtures & soft clustering
nodes.text: Represent a distribution as weighted Gaussian components with latent assignments, means and covariance structure.
nodes.handle: Generalize hard clustering with soft assignments and explicit distributional components. [Reference](https://scikit-learn.org/stable/modules/mixture.html)
nodes.boundary: Components need not be physical regimes; covariance collapse and local optima require attention. [Scope](https://scikit-learn.org/stable/modules/mixture.html)
nodes.test: Compare k-means, GMM and supervised regimes for forecasting and correction under overlapping modes.

nodes.name: Expectation maximization & latent-variable fitting
nodes.text: Alternate inference about latent assignments or sufficient statistics with parameter fitting; GMMs and HMMs provide concrete examples.
nodes.handle: Separate state/assignment inference from parameter estimation in a structured learning loop. [Reference](https://scikit-learn.org/stable/modules/mixture.html)
nodes.boundary: The tested procedure is not guaranteed to find the global optimum; unbounded likelihoods can occur in unregularized mixtures. [Scope](https://scikit-learn.org/stable/modules/mixture.html)
nodes.test: Compare restarts, held-out likelihood, recovered regimes and downstream action utility, not training likelihood alone.

nodes.name: Bootstrap & sampling uncertainty
nodes.authors: Bradley Efron · Robert Tibshirani (1993 reference); SciPy community
nodes.text: Resampling estimates variability of a statistic and can construct approximate confidence intervals.
nodes.handle: Report uncertainty on performance differences instead of ranking methods by a single run. [Reference](https://docs.scipy.org/doc/scipy/reference/generated/scipy.stats.bootstrap.html)
nodes.boundary: Resampling must respect the data-generating structure; ordinary row resampling is not automatically valid for dependent trajectories. [Scope](https://docs.scipy.org/doc/scipy/reference/generated/scipy.stats.bootstrap.html)
nodes.test: Resample independent experimental units or trajectories and check coverage in controlled simulations.

nodes.name: Conformal prediction & coverage
nodes.authors: Anastasios Angelopoulos · Rina Foygel Barber · Stephen Bates
nodes.text: Calibrate prediction sets with finite-sample marginal coverage under exchangeability and the specified construction.
nodes.handle: Wrap a predictor with a measured uncertainty set while separating set size from coverage. [Reference](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2411.11824v4)
nodes.boundary: Marginal coverage is not per-input correctness, adaptive-trajectory safety or protection against arbitrary distribution shift. [Scope](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2411.11824v4)
nodes.test: Test coverage by horizon, subgroup and shifted policy; report failures of exchangeability rather than assume the theorem still applies.

nodes.name: Proper scoring rules & calibration
nodes.text: Score full predictive distributions with rules that reward truthful distributions in expectation under stated conditions.
nodes.handle: Use log score, CRPS or energy scores rather than point error alone to compare probabilistic forecasts. [Reference](https://sites.stat.washington.edu/raftery/Research/PDF/Gneiting2007jasa.pdf)
nodes.boundary: Proper scoring is an evaluation property, not evidence that a trained model is calibrated, causal or aligned. [Scope](https://sites.stat.washington.edu/raftery/Research/PDF/Gneiting2007jasa.pdf)
nodes.test: Compare calibration and sharpness by horizon and regime, then separately measure decisions made from those forecasts.

nodes.name: Online uncertainty under distribution shift
nodes.text: Adapt conformal thresholds online; the cited work establishes local-interval regret results under its stated setup.
nodes.handle: Track changing forecast errors rather than assume a fixed calibration distribution. [Reference](https://www.jmlr.org/papers/v25/22-1218.html)
nodes.boundary: Online regret or long-run error control does not guarantee every next action is safe; transient and rare-event failures remain relevant. [Scope](https://www.jmlr.org/papers/v25/22-1218.html)
nodes.test: Introduce abrupt regime and policy changes; measure transient misses, set sizes and decision consequences.

nodes.name: Probabilistic graphical models
nodes.text: Represent a probability distribution through graph-structured factorization and conditional independence.
nodes.handle: Make uncertainty dependencies and inference assumptions explicit across perception, state, action and objective variables. [Reference](https://people.eecs.berkeley.edu/~jordan/papers/wainwright-jordan-fnt.pdf)
nodes.boundary: A probabilistic graph does not acquire causal intervention semantics merely by drawing arrows. [Scope](https://people.eecs.berkeley.edu/~jordan/papers/wainwright-jordan-fnt.pdf)
nodes.test: Test conditional-independence assumptions and intervention predictions separately from observational likelihood.

nodes.name: Bayesian networks
nodes.text: A directed acyclic graph factorizes a joint distribution into local conditional distributions.
nodes.handle: Build explicit observation, state and objective dependencies with modular conditional models. [Reference](https://people.eecs.berkeley.edu/~jordan/papers/wainwright-jordan-fnt.pdf)
nodes.boundary: Observationally equivalent structures can differ causally; causal use requires additional assumptions or interventions. [Scope](https://people.eecs.berkeley.edu/~jordan/papers/wainwright-jordan-fnt.pdf)
nodes.test: Compare candidate factorizations using held-out interventions, not only fits to passive data.

nodes.name: Markov random fields & Gibbs potentials
nodes.text: Undirected graphs represent distributions through local compatibility factors, including Ising-style pairwise interactions.
nodes.handle: Connect image models, spatial dependencies, energy-based learning and statistical mechanics. [Reference](https://people.eecs.berkeley.edu/~jordan/papers/wainwright-jordan-fnt.pdf)
nodes.boundary: Normalizing constants and inference can be intractable; an energy function is not a physical conservation law. [Scope](https://people.eecs.berkeley.edu/~jordan/papers/wainwright-jordan-fnt.pdf)
nodes.test: Compare approximate marginals against exact small-system calculations and measure downstream decisions.

nodes.name: Factor graphs
nodes.authors: Frank Kschischang · Brendan Frey · Hans-Andrea Loeliger
nodes.text: A bipartite graph separates variables from the factors of a global function or probability distribution.
nodes.handle: Express filtering, decoding and selected transform algorithms through a common factorization language. [Reference](https://cba.mit.edu/events/03.11.ASE/docs/Loeliger.pdf)
nodes.boundary: The factorization specifies a mathematical model, not the correctness of its semantics or assumptions. [Scope](https://cba.mit.edu/events/03.11.ASE/docs/Loeliger.pdf)
nodes.test: Verify messages against direct marginalization on a small model before using approximate large-scale inference.

nodes.name: Belief propagation & sum-product
nodes.text: Pass local messages to compute marginals; finite cycle-free factor graphs admit exact sum-product inference.
nodes.handle: Unify forward-backward, Gaussian filtering and communication-code inference at the algorithmic level. [Reference](https://cba.mit.edu/events/03.11.ASE/docs/Loeliger.pdf)
nodes.boundary: Loopy belief propagation need not converge or return exact marginals; message passing in a GNN is not automatically Bayesian inference. [Scope](https://cba.mit.edu/events/03.11.ASE/docs/Loeliger.pdf)
nodes.test: Measure approximation error and convergence on the actual graph topology and compare with exact or sampling baselines.

nodes.name: Dynamic Bayesian networks
nodes.text: Factor a sequential distribution across time and within each time slice, with hidden states and observations.
nodes.handle: Express HMMs, linear-Gaussian state models and richer switching/factored dynamics within one representation. [Reference](https://www.cs.ubc.ca/~murphyk/Thesis/thesis_double.pdf)
nodes.boundary: Compact representation does not ensure efficient exact inference, identifiable latents or causal action models. [Scope](https://www.cs.ubc.ca/~murphyk/Thesis/thesis_double.pdf)
nodes.test: Compare inferred beliefs and multi-step predictions under missing sensors, switched regimes and unseen actions.

nodes.name: Hidden Markov models & switching regimes
nodes.text: Discrete latent states evolve by a Markov transition model and generate observations; forward-backward supports inference.
nodes.handle: Provide an explicit regime and memory baseline against generic recurrent latent models. [Reference](https://www.cs.ubc.ca/~murphyk/Thesis/thesis_double.pdf)
nodes.boundary: A fitted discrete regime need not correspond to a real cause; its state count and Markov assumptions need validation. [Scope](https://www.cs.ubc.ca/~murphyk/Thesis/thesis_double.pdf)
nodes.test: Test regime recovery, forecast likelihood and action response against ARIMA and neural state models.

nodes.name: Variational inference & statistical free energy
nodes.text: Optimize over a tractable distribution family to approximate inference, with entropy and log-partition duality.
nodes.handle: Link mean-field approximations, probabilistic graphical models and latent-model objectives. [Reference](https://people.eecs.berkeley.edu/~jordan/papers/wainwright-jordan-fnt.pdf)
nodes.boundary: An ELBO is not physical work or an alignment objective; approximation error depends on the variational family. [Scope](https://people.eecs.berkeley.edu/~jordan/papers/wainwright-jordan-fnt.pdf)
nodes.test: Compare posterior moments and downstream decisions with exact or better-sampled reference distributions.

nodes.name: POMDPs & belief-state planning
nodes.authors: Hafner et al.; Hadfield-Menell · Dragan · Abbeel · Russell
nodes.text: Plan with partial observations using a belief over hidden state rather than treating the latest observation as complete state.
nodes.handle: Combine an observation model, action-conditioned dynamics and reward model with sequential inference and planning. [Reference](https://proceedings.mlr.press/v97/hafner19a/hafner19a.pdf)
nodes.boundary: The model, reward and belief update can all be wrong; belief-state sufficiency is conditional on the specified model. [Scope](https://proceedings.mlr.press/v97/hafner19a/hafner19a.pdf)
nodes.test: Require competent long-horizon action selection under ambiguity, information-gathering actions and objective corrections.

nodes.name: Predictive state representations
nodes.authors: Michael Littman · Richard Sutton · Satinder Singh
nodes.year: Foundational paper; year not in fetched text
nodes.text: Represent state by probabilities of future observation tests conditional on specified action sequences.
nodes.handle: A finite POMDP admits a linear PSR with no more core tests than its minimal POMDP state count. [Reference](https://web.eecs.umich.edu/~baveja/Papers/psr.pdf)
nodes.boundary: The representation theorem does not show easy learning, correct causal identification or human-readable semantics. [Scope](https://web.eecs.umich.edu/~baveja/Papers/psr.pdf)
nodes.test: Learn predictive states and test untrained action sequences, rare events and correction retention.

nodes.name: ARIMA & autoregressive forecasting
nodes.authors: Rob Hyndman · George Athanasopoulos; Hyndman · Khandakar
nodes.text: Use autoregression, differencing and moving-average innovations to model time-series dependence.
nodes.handle: Provide transparent temporal baselines with residual diagnostics, stationarity and invertibility checks. [Reference](https://otexts.com/fpp3/arima-r.html)
nodes.boundary: Passive forecasts do not identify effects of a new policy; order selection and regime changes matter. [Scope](https://otexts.com/fpp3/arima-r.html)
nodes.test: Compare multi-horizon forecasts against naive, ETS and neural baselines using time-ordered evaluation.

nodes.name: ETS & innovations state-space forecasting
nodes.text: Represent level, trend and seasonality with stochastic state and observation equations sharing innovations.
nodes.handle: Connect exponential smoothing to model-based forecast distributions rather than point updates alone. [Reference](https://robjhyndman.com/nyc2018/1-5-StateSpace.pdf)
nodes.boundary: Equal point forecasts can have different uncertainty; level and trend are not automatically physical latent variables. [Scope](https://robjhyndman.com/nyc2018/1-5-StateSpace.pdf)
nodes.test: Compare point error and interval quality at several horizons, including abrupt changes in seasonality.

nodes.name: Forecast backtesting & horizon evaluation
nodes.text: Evaluate forecasts on successive future windows using only the information available at each forecast origin.
nodes.handle: Keep chronological train/test boundaries and compare error separately for each horizon. [Reference](https://robjhyndman.com/hyndsight/tscv-fable/)
nodes.boundary: Backtesting under one data-collection policy does not establish validity under a new intervention policy. [Scope](https://robjhyndman.com/hyndsight/tscv-fable/)
nodes.test: Audit leakage, observation delays, repeated tuning and future-covariate availability.

nodes.name: Physical forecasting & learned simulators
nodes.text: Learn multi-step physical forecasts from historical/reanalysis states; GraphCast supplies a concrete weather example.
nodes.handle: Separate multi-step forecast accuracy from the cost and fidelity of a physical simulator. [Reference](https://www.science.org/doi/10.1126/science.adi2336)
nodes.boundary: A strong passive forecast is not a validated controlled world model or a causal simulator for arbitrary interventions. [Scope](https://www.science.org/doi/10.1126/science.adi2336)
nodes.test: Evaluate forecast horizons, rare events, sensor shifts and any claimed action effects as separate tasks.

nodes.name: Horizon-aware world-model uncertainty
nodes.authors: Shenghua Wan · Le Gan · De-Chuan Zhan
nodes.text: Pretrain a probabilistic ensemble over varying forecast horizons, then learn an action-conditioned stream for downstream control.
nodes.handle: The HAUWM paper tests a horizon-dependent disagreement objective and downstream control performance. [Reference](https://proceedings.iclr.cc/paper_files/paper/2026/file/ad222e6e38e26e3f00d85829b9e02f43-Paper-Conference.pdf)
nodes.boundary: Ensemble disagreement is not a calibrated-coverage theorem. Action-free video does not itself identify action effects. [Scope](https://proceedings.iclr.cc/paper_files/paper/2026/file/ad222e6e38e26e3f00d85829b9e02f43-Paper-Conference.pdf)
nodes.test: Compare uncertainty with empirical errors by horizon and action regime, then test whether it improves decisions.

nodes.name: Maximum entropy & Gibbs distributions
nodes.text: Moment constraints and entropy optimization connect exponential-family distributions, partition functions and statistical mechanics.
nodes.handle: Specify which statistics a model preserves instead of treating maximum entropy as assumption-free ignorance. [Reference](https://people.eecs.berkeley.edu/~jordan/papers/wainwright-jordan-fnt.pdf)
nodes.boundary: The chosen constraints encode modeling decisions. A mathematical inverse-temperature parameter need not be physical temperature. [Scope](https://people.eecs.berkeley.edu/~jordan/papers/wainwright-jordan-fnt.pdf)
nodes.test: Change preserved statistics and test sensitivity of predictions, uncertainty and task decisions.

nodes.name: Statistical susceptibility & response covariance
nodes.text: Derivatives of an exponential-family log partition function yield expected sufficient statistics and their covariance.
nodes.handle: For fixed support and a regular normalizable family, response derivatives provide exact local sensitivity identities. [Reference](https://people.eecs.berkeley.edu/~jordan/papers/wainwright-jordan-fnt.pdf)
nodes.boundary: A Gibbs/posterior response is not the same object as a finite optimizer trajectory or arbitrary causal intervention. [Scope](https://people.eecs.berkeley.edu/~jordan/papers/wainwright-jordan-fnt.pdf)
nodes.test: Compare predicted local response with actual finite perturbations and separately test retrained-model response.

nodes.name: Langevin dynamics & posterior sampling
nodes.text: Combine gradients with controlled Gaussian noise to approach posterior sampling under appropriate limiting conditions.
nodes.handle: Connect stochastic dynamics and Bayesian learning; the noise schedule and step size are part of the method. [Reference](https://www.stats.ox.ac.uk/~teh/research/compstats/WelTeh2011a.pdf)
nodes.boundary: Finite-step bias, mixing and gradient noise matter. Ordinary SGD or Adam is not automatically an equilibrium sampler. [Scope](https://www.stats.ox.ac.uk/~teh/research/compstats/WelTeh2011a.pdf)
nodes.test: Check effective sample size and between-chain agreement before using posterior response estimates to choose interventions.

nodes.name: Mori–Zwanzig memory & closure
nodes.authors: Xander de Wit · Alessandro Gabbana · Michael Woodward · Yen Ting Lin · Federico Toschi · Daniel Livescu
nodes.text: Projecting dynamics onto resolved variables leaves instantaneous dynamics, history-dependent memory and unresolved forcing.
nodes.handle: The cited turbulence model learns finite-memory operators and tests long-time statistics. [Reference](https://arxiv.org/html/2507.16058v1)
nodes.boundary: Truncating memory or discarding unresolved forcing is an approximation; passive turbulence results do not establish controlled semantic dynamics. [Scope](https://arxiv.org/html/2507.16058v1)
nodes.test: Compare Markov, delay-state and learned-memory models on multi-step prediction, regime shifts and controlled interventions.

nodes.name: Computational mechanics & predictive states
nodes.authors: Cosma Rohilla Shalizi · James P. Crutchfield
nodes.text: Group histories that induce the same distribution of futures; predictive states minimize stored statistical complexity under stated conditions.
nodes.handle: Connect state construction, past-future information and sufficient prediction for stationary symbolic processes. [Reference](https://arxiv.org/pdf/cs/0001027v1)
nodes.boundary: The term causal state here means predictive equivalence, not automatically an intervention variable or physical state. [Scope](https://arxiv.org/pdf/cs/0001027v1)
nodes.test: Test approximate predictive-state sufficiency and then separately test action-conditioned and nonstationary generalization.

nodes.name: Thermodynamics of prediction
nodes.authors: Susanne Still · David Sivak · Anthony Bell · Gavin Crooks
nodes.text: Relate nonpredictive memory to physical dissipation in a specified driven system coupled to a heat bath.
nodes.handle: The work provides a real information/physics bridge with physical inverse temperature and a stated protocol. [Reference](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1203.3271)
nodes.boundary: The result assumes no feedback from the system to its driving signal. It is not an energy law for arbitrary neural training or a moral objective. [Scope](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1203.3271)
nodes.test: Verify the physical setup before testing an energy relation; otherwise treat neural-system transfer as an explicit hypothesis.

nodes.name: Assistance games & uncertain human objectives
nodes.authors: Dylan Hadfield-Menell · Anca Dragan · Pieter Abbeel · Stuart Russell
nodes.text: Model cooperation with a human whose reward parameter is initially unknown to the machine; communication and teaching can matter.
nodes.handle: CIRL connects objective uncertainty with a coordination POMDP and active information gathering. [Reference](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1606.03137)
nodes.boundary: A shared, representable reward and a specified human model are assumptions, not proof that real intentions are recovered. [Scope](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1606.03137)
nodes.test: Test clarification, corrections and deference under ambiguous instructions, mistaken feedback and conflicting stakeholders.

nodes.name: Proxy objectives & reward misspecification
nodes.authors: Joar Skalse · Nikolaus Howe · Dmitrii Krasheninnikov · David Krueger
nodes.text: Analyze when increasing proxy return can reverse the ordering induced by a true reward within a specified policy set.
nodes.handle: Check the policy set and evaluate true task outcomes rather than treating a learned reward as a complete specification. [Reference](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2209.13085)
nodes.boundary: The finite-MDP ordering theorem does not prove hacking occurs on every actual training trajectory. [Scope](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2209.13085)
nodes.test: Optimize against the proxy deliberately and test for rising proxy score with falling independently measured user utility.

nodes.name: Alignment thesis: capable, correctable belief-state systems
nodes.text: Construct useful representations, action-conditioned models and correction interfaces; retain uncertainty about intent and separately enforce execution authority.
nodes.sourceLabel: Related foundation: CIRL, not proof of this thesis
nodes.handle: Proposed integration: observation integrity, belief state, consequence forecasting, objective uncertainty, correctable planning, and validated learning updates. [Reference](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1606.03137)
nodes.boundary: No cited source proves this composition solves alignment. The main missing transfer is from validated component models to persistent, semantically correct behavior under strategic distribution shift. [Scope](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1606.03137)
nodes.test: Require a substantive capability plus correction benefit over predeclared simple baselines, across unseen tasks, policy shifts and adversarial feedback.

nodes.name: Markov chain Monte Carlo & Metropolis–Hastings
nodes.authors: Metropolis et al. · Hastings; Andrieu · de Freitas · Doucet · Jordan (reference)
nodes.text: Build a Markov chain whose invariant distribution is the target: propose x′ ~ q(x′|x) and accept with probability min{1, p(x′)q(x|x′) / p(x)q(x′|x)}, so the normalizing constant cancels.
nodes.handle: Treat samplers as transition kernels with a known invariant law, so cycles and mixtures of valid kernels stay valid. [Reference](https://www.cs.ubc.ca/~arnaud/andrieu_defreitas_doucet_jordan_intromontecarlomachinelearning.pdf)
nodes.boundary: Invariance is not practical convergence: finite runs can miss modes, and slow mixing need not show in a single chain's trace. [Scope](https://www.cs.ubc.ca/~arnaud/andrieu_defreitas_doucet_jordan_intromontecarlomachinelearning.pdf)
nodes.test: Run several dispersed chains; compare between-chain agreement and effective sample size against an exactly computable small case.

nodes.name: Gibbs sampling
nodes.authors: Stuart Geman · Donald Geman; Alan Gelfand · Adrian Smith
nodes.text: Redraw one variable or site at a time from its full conditional given all the others. On a Markov random field each draw needs only the neighbors, never the partition function.
nodes.handle: Turn a joint posterior or Gibbs distribution into local conditional draws, easy whenever the model is discrete or conditionally conjugate. [Reference](https://cs.uwaterloo.ca/~mannr/cs886-w10/GemanandGeman84.pdf)
nodes.boundary: Strongly coupled coordinates, such as correlated parameters or low temperature, make one-at-a-time updates mix slowly; sampling is not MAP estimation without annealing. [Scope](https://www.cs.ubc.ca/~arnaud/andrieu_defreitas_doucet_jordan_intromontecarlomachinelearning.pdf)
nodes.test: Measure autocorrelation and effective sample size per second against a blocked or collapsed variant on the same model.

nodes.name: Blocked & collapsed Gibbs; forward-filtering backward-sampling
nodes.authors: Liu · Wong · Kong; Jun Liu; Carter · Kohn; Frühwirth-Schnatter
nodes.text: Update dependent variables jointly, or integrate some out before sampling. In HMMs and linear-Gaussian state-space models a forward filter plus backward sampling draws the whole latent path as one block.
nodes.handle: Embed exact sub-inference, such as forward filtering or conjugate marginalization, inside a sampler to cut autocorrelation. [Reference](https://www.cs.columbia.edu/~blei/fogm/2023F/readings/Liu1994.pdf)
nodes.boundary: The proven ordering covers specific nested grouping and collapsing schemes; it does not show every blocking helps, and a joint draw can cost more per sweep than it saves. [Scope](https://www.cs.columbia.edu/~blei/fogm/2023F/readings/Liu1994.pdf)
nodes.test: Compare integrated autocorrelation time per unit compute for single-site, blocked and collapsed samplers on one posterior.

nodes.name: Particle MCMC & particle Gibbs
nodes.authors: Christophe Andrieu · Arnaud Doucet · Roman Holenstein
nodes.text: Use a sequential Monte Carlo sweep inside MCMC. A conditional SMC update that keeps one reference path alive gives a Gibbs sampler for parameters and latent paths of nonlinear state-space models.
nodes.handle: Put particle filters inside samplers whose invariant law is the exact posterior p(θ, x₁:T | y₁:T) for a finite particle count. [Reference](https://www.stats.ox.ac.uk/~doucet/andrieu_doucet_holenstein_PMCMC.pdf)
nodes.boundary: Exactness concerns the invariant law, not mixing: with too few particles for the series length, path degeneracy makes the chain stick. [Scope](https://www.stats.ox.ac.uk/~doucet/andrieu_doucet_holenstein_PMCMC.pdf)
nodes.test: Vary particle count against series length; track update rates of early states and autocorrelation of θ.
